Also, every core step uses ONLY_ON_DEVICE or ONLY_IN_CLOUD and never the SDK's automatic fallback, so a judge could read it as 'two separate models' rather than hybrid inference. On iOS the Hypothesizer has to bypass HybridModel entirely and call the system model directly, because HybridModel automatically sends the request to the cloud when the on-device model is unavailable.

The architecture is not new. Pseudonymize, send to an LLM, then re-identify locally is the same PHI firewall as the Muganga baseline. It is also an established enterprise pattern: Microsoft Presidio reversible anonymization, LLM Guard Anonymize/Deanonymize, LangChain OpaquePrompts, Private AI's PrivateGPT and Google Cloud DLP re-identification. All the novelty sits in the 'legal hypothetical' framing and the rehydrated letter.

Legal-harm and regulatory risk. Search grounding reduces errors but does not remove them: a wrong limitation period turns into a wrong deadline countdown for a vulnerable person. The FTC's DoNotPay order ('robot lawyer', 2024-25) shows how regulators treat AI legal tools that make strong claims. Every fact in the demo (the Ontario ESA wage-claim limit and reprisal protection; English deposit-protection rules) has to be checked by hand.

Scope against the 11 days. Capability corrections found in those docs:
(1) On iOS, on-device-only IS possible: call ai.generativeModelSession(model: systemModel) without a HybridModel and it throws instead of falling back. HybridModel with on-device primary falls back to cloud automatically, which must not happen for the raw story. Inference source is readable from response.rawResponse.modelVersion.
(2) The iOS docs now list structured output and function calling as supported on-device, but say the docs for both are 'coming soon' and contradict each other. Treat both as unverified.
(3) Server prompt templates, Live API and countTokens are not supported in any hybrid setup. Using Remote Config for prompts is fine.

red.mitigations:
1. Never let the privacy guarantee depend on the model being present. Use three local tiers:
- Tier 0 (every device): deterministic rules. Regex for money, dates, phones, emails and postcodes; a small NER library such as compromise.js; gazetteers that map city to province or state. The user can tap any word to hide it.
- Tier 1: the Nano or Foundation Models Hypothesizer.
- No tier sends the raw text to the cloud. Show that as the guarantee on screen.

2. Make the LLM extract, not rewrite. The on-device model returns a JSON table of entities: {span, type, role, keep_as: range|relative|jurisdiction|drop}. Code then does the substitution and a leak check (no original token may survive) before Send is enabled. The user approves the diff. Drop the 'uniqueness' AI claim, or replace it with a rule-based quasi-identifier counter: small-town location, rare job, nationality, exact dates.

3. Give judges a working path:
- A 'Try a sample case' button that loads a fictional story, is allowed to use PREFER_ON_DEVICE with cloud fallback, and carries a red 'sample data' badge.
- A first-run capability panel showing what runs where, with live inferenceSource badges.
- Day-1 check of whether Chrome 157 still needs the flag (Chrome docs list the web Prompt API as 'Chrome 148, Intent to Ship'). Test in a fresh profile.
- Optionally, a Chrome side-panel extension, since the Prompt API is stable in extensions from Chrome 138. Only if App Check can be made to work there.
- In the video, show the on-device badge clearly on both platforms.

4. Show real hybrid routing where it is safe. Use PREFER_ON_DEVICE for steps after anonymization: problem-type and jurisdiction classification, generating clarifying questions from the hypothetical, and simplifying or translating the cloud answer into a checklist. Judges then see the SDK's automatic fallback as well as the deliberate sensitivity routing. Pitch it as 'routing by data sensitivity, not just availability'. On iOS, use the system model directly for the Hypothesizer and HybridModel only for non-sensitive steps.

5. Be honest about the parts that are code. The cloud returns deadline rules as structured data: {anchor: 'notice_received', offset: 14, unit: 'days'}. On-device AI only extracts the anchor date and amounts from evidence (Nano image input on web; Vision OCR into text on iOS). Code does the date math and the letter fill, and the pitch says so.

6. Fix the claims. Say: 'Your story never leaves this device; what the AI provider receives can't be tied to you by its content.' Never say 'privileged'. Subpoena View should show the hypothetical, the generated Search queries, and the metadata (IP, anonymous UID). Turn off AI monitoring for the grounded call, or disclose the 30-day logs. Add local encryption and a one-tap 'burn this case'. Read the Heppner opinion before citing it. Supporting hooks to verify: the May 2025 preservation order in NYT v. OpenAI, and Sam Altman's July 2025 remark that ChatGPT chats aren't legally confidential.

7. Reposition the primary user so the devices make sense: non-lawyer helpers on desktop Chrome, such as tenant organizers, worker-center staff, court navigators, librarians and legal-aid intake volunteers. They handle other people's confidential stories and can't paste them into ChatGPT. Individuals with recent iPhones or laptops become the secondary user. This keeps the pitch global and matches the 'Best Web' prize.

8. Cut scope:
- Three problem types (unpaid wages, deposit, debt collector) in three hand-verified jurisdictions, for example Ontario, England and California or Germany.
- Drop the curated Firestore directory, or seed about 10 entries and get referrals from grounded search.
- Use two cloud calls: a grounded call that renders searchEntryPoint and the sources, then a JSON-schema call. Don't rely on tools and a schema in one request.
- On iOS, skip tool calls unless they work on day 1. Pass the Vision OCR text straight into the prompt, and limit on-device multi-turn to 3 questions to stay under the 4,096-token limit.

9. Day-1 and day-2 kill checks:
- (a) Does Gemini Nano load in Chrome 157 on this 8 GB M1 with 22 GB of free disk? Check chrome://on-device-internals.
- (b) Does Foundation Models answer through Firebase SDK 12.13+ in the iOS Simulator?
- (c) Does Google Search grounding work through the Firebase JS SDK?
- If (a) fails: go iOS-first and record the web part on a borrowed machine.
- If (b) fails: ship web only and aim for Best Web.

10. Schedule:
- Days 1-2: spikes and the Tier-0/Tier-1 Hypothesizer.
- Days 3-5: web flow (diff, grounded answer, letter, countdown, evidence).
- Days 6-8: iOS subset (Hypothesizer, clarifying questions, cloud, rehydrate).
- Day 9: polish and legal fact-check.
- Day 10: video and write-up.
- Day 11: buffer.

Run Chrome-Nano and the Simulator in separate sessions to avoid memory pressure on the 8 GB machine.

Verdict: the hybrid split is honest and essential, and the demo moment is strong. The idea survives only if the privacy guarantee works without a model (Tier 0) and the pitch stops overclaiming legal protection.

demo.storyboard:
Total 3:00. Record the on-device beats on iOS first: the Foundation Models simulator on this M1 is verified, while Chrome Nano on 8 GB is not. Keep a persistent corner badge on screen, "ON-DEVICE · 0 bytes sent" (green) or "IN CLOUD · Gemini + Search" (blue), driven by response.inferenceSource. Toggle Wi-Fi from the visible macOS menu bar so the switch to offline is plainly real.

BEAT 1 (0:00-0:20) The hook: "Your AI chat can become evidence." Cold open on a generic chatbot window as someone types a real story with real names. A red "EXHIBIT A" stamp slams onto the chat log. VO: "In 2026 a US federal judge ruled that a defendant's AI chats were not privileged. Lawyers have always had a workaround. They say 'asking for a friend.'" Title card: ASKING FOR A FRIEND. (The Heppner reference needs verification first. If it can't be verified, open on "Your chat logs are stored. Anything stored can be subpoenaed.")

BEAT 2 (0:20-0:55) The confession, offline. Web PWA in Chrome with Wi-Fi visibly OFF. The user types the Spanish-English Toronto wage story and taps "Make it hypothetical". A diff animates line by line. Marco becomes Employer, Pizzeria Roma becomes [a restaurant], Toronto becomes Ontario, Canada and $2,340 becomes ~$2,300. The immigration threat stays, marked with a "Kept: the law depends on this" chip. A uniqueness meter reads LOW. The badge stays green the whole time. One tap restores a dropped fact, to show the user is in control.

BEAT 3 (0:55-1:10) Subpoena View, the screenshot people will share. The toggle dims the whole app except one grey paragraph. VO: "This is everything the AI provider could ever hand over. No name, no employer, no account." Cut for half a second to DevTools > Network, where the request body matches that paragraph byte for byte. Wi-Fi goes back ON.

BEAT 4 (1:10-1:45) The grounded answer. The badge turns blue as rights cards stream in: unpaid-wage claim, protection against reprisal for the immigration threat, and the time limit stated as a rule. Each card carries an ontario.ca link chip, and any claim without grounding is greyed out and marked as such. An options ladder fills in: negotiate, demand letter, ministry claim, then a legal clinic near you (pulled from the Firestore directory). The cloud then asks one item from its facts checklist, "Do you have pay stubs?", and the user answers in a single tap, which gets abstracted on-device again. A Spanish toggle re-renders the answer.

BEAT 5 (1:45-2:15) Rehydration, the payoff. Show the cloud letter with {{EMPLOYER_NAME}}, {{BUSINESS}} and {{AMOUNT_OWED}} highlighted, then turn Wi-Fi OFF again. The user photographs a payslip and the evidence locker reads the last pay date on-device. Tap "Make it mine" and the placeholders flip, with a satisfying animation, to Marco, Pizzeria Roma and $2,340. The rule "within N days" becomes a real date, and a countdown chip appears: "Send by Dec 4 · 15 days". Add to calendar. The badge is green the whole way through.

BEAT 6 (2:15-2:45) Global and multi-platform. On iPhone, a London tenant photographs a deposit deduction notice. Foundation Models asks one on-device clarifying question ("Was your deposit registered in a protection scheme?"), and the cloud returns rights with gov.uk links. Then a 5-second cut to a German Kaution case answered in German. A globe drops 3 pins. Overlay the routing table that explains the hybrid design: "Raw story: ONLY_ON_DEVICE. Already anonymous: PREFER_ON_DEVICE. Current law: ONLY_IN_CLOUD."

BEAT 7 (2:45-3:00) Close. "5.1 billion people have an unmet justice need" (World Justice Project). "No lawyer? Ask for a friend." Show the hosted URL with a line saying it works in any browser and that with no local AI it still never sends your story. A strip of Firebase stack logos: AI Logic hybrid, App Check, Remote Config, Anonymous Auth, Firestore, Hosting.

GROWTH: The title, the "Subpoena View" toggle and the EXHIBIT A stamp are each built to be shared, so use one of them as the YouTube thumbnail. The pitch should name legal-aid clinics, worker centers and tenant unions as the distribution channel, which supports the impact score.
demo.weak_spots:
1) JUDGE TRYABILITY IS THE BIGGEST GAP AS SPECCED. The Hypothesizer is ONLY_ON_DEVICE, so a judge without Nano hits a dead end at the hero feature. Most judges will lack Nano: they may be on Safari or Firefox, mobile, or a low-RAM laptop, or the multi-GB model may still be downloading. The fix is to turn the refusal into a feature: "No local AI on this browser, so we will NOT send your story to the cloud." Then offer two paths. (a) A deterministic in-browser fallback redactor: regex for money, dates, phone numbers, emails and addresses, plus compromise.js or a small transformers.js NER model for names, plus a city-to-jurisdiction gazetteer, all feeding the same diff UI. (b) Three one-tap sample cases with cached on-device output. Rehydration and deadline math are deterministic placeholder substitution and date arithmetic, so they work for everyone, and the grounded cloud answer works for everyone too. With that fallback tryability is about 7; without it, about 4.

2) HARDWARE RISK FOR THE RECORDING. Chrome's Gemini Nano requirements (a GPU with more than 4 GB VRAM, or 16 GB RAM for CPU) may exclude an 8 GB M1. Verify on day 1. If it fails, iOS Foundation Models carries every on-device beat, and the web build is shown on the fallback path or recorded on borrowed hardware.

3) THE PRIVACY CLAIM MUST BE SCRUPULOUSLY HONEST, OR A JUDGE WILL CATCH IT. The cloud request still carries an IP address, an App Check token and an anonymous UID. "Subpoena View" should therefore say "content contains nothing identifying," not "nothing about you." The cloud path should use the Vertex AI Gemini backend or a paid tier, not the free Developer API, whose data may be used for model improvement. Search grounding also sends a derived query to Google Search, so disclose that. Say "not linkable to you," never "privileged."

4) THE HOOK RESTS ON AN UNVERIFIED CASE. My recollection is that in early 2026 Judge Rakoff in US v. Heppner (S.D.N.Y.) held that a criminal defendant's AI-generated materials were not privileged. The web search budget was exhausted in this run, so this is NOT verified. Check the docket and holding before citing it, and don't generalize a criminal-case ruling into "every chat is subpoenable everywhere."

5) IT CAN LOOK LIKE "JUST A PII REDACTOR," A KNOWN IDEA. Lead every frame with the legal outcome: rights, deadline and letter. Present redaction as the mechanism. Rehydration plus deadline conversion is the non-obvious part, so give it the climax beat.

6) THE ANSWERS ARE TEXT-HEAVY. Grounded legal answers can make for a boring video. They have to be cards, a ladder and chips, not paragraphs. Pre-test that the cloud output is accurate for the Ontario, England and Germany scripts; a hallucinated section number on screen sinks the Impact score. Show grounding links only, and visibly grey out unsupported claims.

7) THE LANGUAGE CLAIM IS NARROWER THAN THE GLOBAL PITCH IMPLIES. On-device language coverage is limited: Chrome Nano supports roughly English, Spanish and Japanese, Android is validated only for English and Korean, and Apple FM is broader. Code-switched Spanglish input is a live risk, so rehearse it or have a fallback take. The privacy layer is therefore global in principle but multilingual only in a handful of languages, while the cloud answer is multilingual.

8) THE GLOBAL STORY IS UNEVEN. Grounding quality is strongest in English and EU common-law jurisdictions and weakest exactly where justice gaps are largest. Remote Config jurisdiction packs make the 3 demo jurisdictions look curated rather than cherry-picked. Say so.

9) SCOPE AND TIME. Two platforms, an evidence locker with OCR, a re-ask loop, Firestore legal-aid data and 3 jurisdictions in 11 days is a lot for one agent. Cut Android entirely (or make it cloud-only and keep it out of the video). Limit the evidence locker to one document type per problem.

10) UNAUTHORIZED-PRACTICE AND HARM OPTICS. The immigration-threat example is powerful but sensitive. Add an explicit "legal information, not advice" line and a legal-aid handoff in the UI, and make sure no generated letter could worsen a vulnerable user's situation (for example, add a "talk to a clinic before sending" gate on reprisal cases).

11) THE SMALL-TOWN RE-IDENTIFICATION RISK IS REAL. The uniqueness meter has to actually do something, such as counting rare-fact combinations, not just exist as decoration, or a judge's probe will expose it.

finalist.name: Muganga (baseline)
finalist.pitch: Offline-first clinic copilot for low-connectivity primary-care clinics; on-device structures notes into SOAP + vitals JSON, rule-based danger-sign flags, de-identifies patient data (PHI firewall); cloud only gets de-identified text for referral letters, long-history summaries, translation; re-identification on device; offline job queue; Web + iOS.

judge.rationale: Tech (7): This entry uses hybrid inference for a better reason than most. Routing depends on whether the data is sensitive, not only on whether the model is available. On-device turns notes into SOAP plus vitals JSON (Web supports structured output), applies the de-identification gate, and puts real names back in afterwards. The cloud handles the jobs a small model can't: long histories, referral letters and translation. The offline queue suits the setting. Of the ~300 entries I've seen, it's one of the few where the split between device and cloud carries the design. It drops to 7 for three reasons. Small on-device models miss some names and IDs when redacting, and a single miss breaks the privacy promise. iOS can't do structured output through HybridModel yet, so the two platforms behave differently. And PREFER_ON_DEVICE silently falls back to cloud, which means raw patient data goes to the cloud on any device without a local model unless the builder adds fail-closed logic. Design (6): Even if built well, this is a dense clinical workflow: intake, structuring, danger flags, referral, queue and putting names back. Making that feel complete on two platforms in 11 days is hard. Judges aren't clinicians, so a 3-minute video of SOAP notes is hard to connect with, and the most important moment ('the cloud never saw the name') is invisible unless it's designed to be seen. Impact (6): The audience and problem are real and specific, but the case falls apart under scrutiny. The low-connectivity clinics it targets are the places least likely to have iPhones with Apple Intelligence or Chrome machines that can run Gemini Nano. So the on-device privacy path, the core of the pitch, mostly won't run for the people it's built for. Clinical safety and liability for AI danger flags, plus no evidence of clinician validation, make judges cautious. The Rwanda framing also narrows how broadly it reads. Idea (7): The 'PHI firewall' pattern (device as policy enforcer, cloud as de-identified worker, names restored on device) is clearly non-obvious and shows a real grasp of what hybrid inference makes possible. But 'AI clinic scribe' is familiar from industry products (ambient-scribe tools) and from health-track hackathon entries, so the domain looks less original than the mechanism.
judge.biggest_weakness: The headline promise, that the cloud only ever sees de-identified data, is weakest exactly where it matters. The target users (low-resource clinics) are the least likely to have devices that can run Gemini Nano or Apple Foundation Models. PREFER_ON_DEVICE quietly falls back to cloud with raw text. Small-model redaction misses some names. And most judges will run the hosted app without a local model, so they never see the privacy path work. The best part of the idea is the part least likely to show up in the demo or in the field, and the region-specific health framing adds to that.
judge.best_upgrade: Make the privacy boundary the product, make it fail closed, and pitch it to a global audience. Use ONLY_ON_DEVICE for every step that handles raw identifiers. Back it up with deterministic redaction (regex plus dictionaries for names, IDs, dates, phone numbers) so nothing identifiable goes to the cloud when no local model exists, and block the cloud call when redaction confidence is low. Show a visible 'Cloud Receipt' on every request: the exact text sent, with on-device and in-cloud badges taken from inferenceSource. Then present it as a domain-agnostic pattern for any worldwide professional who handles regulated personal data on their own device, with clinicians as the hero demo. Examples are home-care nurses, social workers and lawyers under HIPAA or GDPR. That fixes the fallback contradiction, gives judges something they can verify without a local model, and removes the regional ceiling.

fatal_flaws: It fails the user's own requirement. The user called it too region-specific and asked why it leans on health. Making it global does not rescue it. In rich-country clinics, cloud ambient scribes covered by a BAA (business associate agreement) already own the problem, so the offline and on-device case is weak. In low-resource clinics, the hardware problem below applies.

The target users' hardware cannot run on-device models. Gemini Nano in Chrome needs more than 4 GB of VRAM, or 16 GB of RAM on CPU, plus about 22 GB of free disk and (per current Firebase docs) a Chrome flag. Android AICore Nano runs only on recent flagships. Apple Foundation Models needs an iPhone 15 Pro or newer, or an M-series Mac. Nurses in low-connectivity primary clinics and community health workers on Tecno, Itel or Samsung A-series phones have none of these. Real users would always take the cloud or regex path. That cancels the offline-first and PHI-firewall pitch, and a judge testing for 'genuine understanding of the problem space' will notice.

The privacy plan has a design bug. PLAN.md routes structuring through PREFER_ON_DEVICE using the RAW note. When no local model is present, which is true for most judges and almost all target users, the full identifiable note (names, phone numbers) goes to cloud Gemini. On iOS, HybridModel(primary:, secondary:) falls back to cloud automatically, which is the opposite of failing closed. Unless the iOS PHI step skips the Firebase hybrid wrapper and calls SystemLanguageModel directly (which makes the iOS hybrid partly decorative), the firewall fails open.

The firewall claim cannot be kept. A roughly 3B on-device model running NER over non-English names (Kinyarwanda or Swahili) in clinician shorthand will miss identifiers, and free-text de-identification is still an open research problem. Quasi-identifiers also survive: '4y F, Kicukiro, fever 3d' in a small catchment area can identify a patient. A '0 identifiers sent' counter is a liability claim that the planned 60 synthetic, LLM-written notes cannot support.

Most judges will not see the headline feature. Without Nano enabled (flag, model download, enough hardware), the hosted app shows only regex redaction plus confirm dialogs. The hybrid story then exists only in the video, which hurts the Technological Implementation and Design scores.

The scope is too large for 11 days. One coding agent would have to build a web PWA (editor, structuring, IMCI rules engine with tests, LLM plus regex firewall, diff UI, router, 3 to 4 cloud tasks, re-identification, offline queue, Firestore persistence, Auth, Remote Config, App Check, Hosting, dashboard, eval harness) and also an iOS app on an Experimental SDK. That has to happen on an 8 GB M1 where Xcode, the Simulator, Apple FM and Chrome Nano (about 4 GB) compete for memory, and on-device testing loops are slow and need a human.

iOS has no on-device structured output. SOAP sections, vitals JSON and findings for the rules engine would need prompted JSON on Apple FM inside a 4,096-token window that also holds the system instructions, schema and examples. Doing PHI detection, structuring and finding extraction as separate calls per note means slow, fragile parsing. The plan's mention of @Generable only works by calling FoundationModels directly, outside Firebase AI Logic.

The novelty is weaker than it looks. Offline IMCI danger-sign logic is long established in Medic's Community Health Toolkit, Dimagi CommCare and Swiss TPH's ePOCT+ (deployed in Tanzania and Rwanda). An LLM copilot for primary care in East Africa has already been studied: Penda Health with OpenAI's 'AI Consult' in Nairobi, 2025. The 'pseudonymize, send to LLM, re-identify' pattern exists in Microsoft Presidio, LangChain's PresidioReversibleAnonymizer, Skyflow's LLM privacy vault, Private AI, Nightfall and LLM Guard. Domain-literate judges may see a re-implementation.

It carries safety and regulatory baggage. Rule-based triage flags shown as an 'URGENT REFERRAL' banner sit close to Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) territory. LLM-translated discharge instructions in Kinyarwanda are a patient-safety risk, with no back-translation or validation. The data is synthetic only, so the Impact claims cannot be checked, and the builder has no clinical domain input to show genuine understanding.

If any part survives, it should be the mechanism, not the clinic product.

(1) Drop the Rwanda and clinic framing, as the user asked. Move the 'on-device firewall, cloud does the work, re-identify on device' mechanism to a global audience that already owns capable hardware: professionals on recent Macs, Chromebook Plus machines or iPhones who handle confidential client data and are barred from pasting it into cloud AI. (3) Scope the claim honestly. Say 'reduces identifiers sent' with a measured leak rate on a published synthetic set, not '0 identifiers sent'. Treat quasi-identifiers (dates becoming relative offsets, locations generalized) as explicit transforms.

Spend Day 0 proving that Nano runs in Chrome on this 8 GB M1 and that Apple FM runs in the Simulator, and pivot that same day if either fails.

(5) Make the hosted demo show the split without Nano. Add a recorded or replayable 'on-device trace' mode, and clear UI that explains which tier ran and why.

The clinician dictates a messy note. iOS on-device speech recognition turns it into text, and Apple Foundation Models through HybridModel turns that into SOAP plus vitals. The badge reads ON-DEVICE, 1.4s, $0. A deterministic danger-sign rule then fires in red: "SpO2 88% + age under 5 -> urgent referral", citing its guideline source. VO: "No signal, no problem, no data left the room."

BEAT 3 (0:50-1:25) THE FIREWALL MOMENT. This is the hero shot. Tap "Draft referral". Name, date of birth, ID number, phone and village light up and animate into tokens such as [PT_1] and [DOB_1]. A panel titled "Exactly what will leave this device" shows the real payload. Because there is no network, the job lands in an offline queue with a chip reading "1 job waiting for network".

BEAT 4 (1:25-1:55) RECONNECT. Airplane mode goes off and the queue flushes. Cloud Gemini (badge: IN CLOUD) writes a full referral letter and translates it into the receiving hospital's language, working only from de-identified text. Back on the device, the tokens snap back into real names locally. Cut to the network inspector, where a search of the outgoing payload for the patient's name returns 0 matches. VO: "The cloud did the heavy lifting and never learned who the patient was."

BEAT 5 (1:55-2:25) SECOND PLATFORM. The same workflow runs on the web in Chrome. If Gemini Nano works on the 8 GB M1, show on-device structuring. If not, show the honest fallback: structuring goes to the cloud with a de-identified payload only, and the deterministic tokenizer guards the boundary. A long multi-visit history summary goes to the cloud because it exceeds the on-device token limit. Remote Config switches the danger-rule pack (for example from a pediatric pack to a maternal pack) live, and the App Check badge is visible.

BEAT 6 (2:25-2:50) WHY HYBRID. One clean architecture card with three rows: on-device handles private, fast, offline work (structure, flag, de-identify, re-identify); cloud handles capable, long and multilingual work (letters, history, translation); the deterministic layer handles guarantees (rules, token map). Close the beat on the hosted URL and its one-click synthetic cases.

BEAT 7 (2:50-3:00) CLOSE. VO: "For any clinician whose patient data can't leave the room, from a rural health post with one bar of signal to a GP under GDPR or HIPAA." Then the logo, URL and repo link.
demo.weak_spots:
1. On a judge's machine the privacy promise can break. Most judges will not have Chrome's Gemini Nano. If the PREFER_ON_DEVICE de-identification step falls back to the cloud, raw patient data goes to Gemini, which is the opposite of the pitch. Fix: never run de-identification through a PREFER_* fallback. Make tokenization deterministic first. The intake form already captures name, date of birth, ID, phone and location as fields, so those values are known exactly and can be swapped for tokens with no model involved. The on-device model only adds catches from free text (ONLY_ON_DEVICE, skipped if unavailable). The hosted demo should show a "firewall active (rules-only mode)" state so the boundary is visibly honest without on-device AI.

2. A judge without a local model gets a weaker version of the core experience. On a hosted URL they will not feel the offline or on-device magic. To compensate: add one-click synthetic cases, a visible payload inspector, a simulated "go offline" toggle that exercises the queue, and inference-source badges. Without these, a judge just sees "another cloud scribe".

3. Global reach is limited by framing, not by the problem. The Rwandan name and East-African clinic story read as regional, and the audience is professional clinicians, not the general public. Rebrand to a neutral name and pitch two audiences at once: community health workers and clinics with poor connectivity worldwide, and privacy-regulated clinicians in the EU and US who cannot paste patient notes into cloud AI. Even then it is a vertical B2B tool, not a mass-market app. On its own it does not meet the user's request for something globally used.

4. Crowding and how obvious it is. Real-world AI scribes (DAX, Abridge and others) are well known to judges, and "PII redactor in front of a chatbot" is already a known hackathon pattern. The non-obvious angle has to be shown very clearly: the device acts as a trust boundary and the cloud acts as a muscle that never sees identity, including re-identification on the device. Without the payload-inspector shot it reads as "redactor plus scribe".

5. Clinical-safety skepticism. Danger-sign flags look like medical advice. Keep them as deterministic, cited rules (for example a WHO IMCI-style pack in Remote Config), label the product as documentation and referral support rather than diagnosis, and use only synthetic patients in the video and the hosted app.

6. Firestore sync contradicts the firewall. Syncing patient records to Firestore puts identifying data in the cloud. Either sync only de-identified or client-side-encrypted records (the token map stays on the device), or skip cross-device patient sync and use Firestore only for job metadata and settings.

7. Platform risk.
   - Chrome Nano on an 8 GB M1 is unverified. If it fails, the web's on-device story collapses, so record the on-device hero shots on the iOS Simulator with Apple Foundation Models, which works on this Mac.
   - Android is cloud-only here, so it is not a real third platform.
   - Through Firebase on iOS, on-device structured output is not supported yet. SOAP JSON on iOS needs function calling or tolerant prompt-and-parse.
   - Web on-device has no multi-turn or audio. Voice dictation must come from iOS on-device speech recognition or the Web Speech API, not from Gemini.
   - Token limits (about 4k on iOS, about 9k on web) push longer notes to the cloud. This is fine because it is part of the hybrid story, but it must happen through the de-identified path.

8. Visual energy. The screens are text-heavy and the domain is serious, so the video depends on three motion moments: the airplane-mode toggle, the PHI-to-token animation, and the tokens snapping back to names. If any one is weak, the score on wow drops to about 4-5.

9. Proof of impact. Judges want a specific number shown on screen, for example "referral letter in 40s vs about 10 min handwritten" or "0 identifiers in N outgoing requests". Measure one real metric on the synthetic set and show it in Beat 4 or Beat 6.

synthesis.winner: Strangers' Eyes: see your photo the way a stalker's AI would, before you post it (the cloud plays the attacker, your device keeps the answers)
synthesis.winner_full_spec:
NAME: Strangers' Eyes
TAGLINE: "See your photo the way a stalker's AI would, before you post it."
ONE-LINER FOR JUDGES: The cloud plays the attacker and your device holds the answers, so the attacker never learns whether it guessed right.

1. TARGET USER
- Anyone who posts photos publicly, about 5B social media users. The threat and the fix are the same in every country and language.
- Hero personas, in demo order: parents posting home and school-run photos; marketplace sellers photographing rooms in their homes (Facebook Marketplace, Vinted, OLX, Mercari, Craigslist); creators and streamers.
- Highest-need users: domestic-violence survivors, journalists, activists.
- Distribution: DV-support organisations, school parent groups, creator communities, and a shareable "AI found my neighbourhood. I fixed it." card that never contains the location.

2. PROBLEM (verify every stat before it goes on screen)
- Stripping GPS no longer protects you. Multimodal models geolocate EXIF-free photos from the pixels alone: street signs, paving and tiles, transit-stop codes, uniforms and lanyard logos, window views, reflections.
- The April 2025 "reverse location search" trend using OpenAI o3 (TechCrunch, Tom's Hardware) made this a party trick. GeoSpy and Picarta sell it. McAfee, a vendor, claims AI located 87-91% of the travel photos it tested.
- A widely reported 2019 Tokyo case: a stalker found a singer's home using reflections in her eyes in a selfie plus street imagery.
- Platforms strip EXIF, so people feel safe. Nobody can see what an adversary could infer, and no tool knows what YOU need to hide.
- Existing defenses fall short:
  - EXIF strippers (Safe Attachment Check, GPSDetect) do nothing about pixels.
  - Research prototypes (arXiv 2503.20226; Geo-Safe-Filter, TikTok TechJam 2025) send your RAW photo to a cloud model and know nothing about your home, workplace or kids' names.
- INSIGHT: attacking a photo needs world knowledge, which only the cloud has. Judging the attack needs your secrets, which should stay on the device. Split the job exactly there.

3. CORE LOOP
Vault (device) -> pre-screen and pre-mask (device) -> red team on a REDACTED copy (cloud) -> referee (device) -> fix (device) -> re-attack (cloud) -> "Risk reduced".

4. ON-DEVICE JOBS: WEB (Chrome, Gemini Nano through the Firebase AI Logic hybrid SDK)
W1 VAULT
- navigator.geolocation "pin this place", captured while physically at home, work or school. Pins are never geocoded by a server.
- Also stores names (kids, self), car plates, house number, employer and school names, and uniform or lanyard descriptors.
- Encrypted in IndexedDB with AES-GCM and a non-extractable WebCrypto key.
- Never synced, never written to Firestore, never put in any prompt that could reach the cloud.

W2 TIER-0 GUARD (deterministic; runs in every browser with no model)
- Strip EXIF/XMP by re-encoding through canvas.
- Self-hosted MediaPipe Face Detector: every face gets a solid mask.
- Tesseract.js OCR on a downscaled image produces word boxes. These are fuzzy-matched (normalised Levenshtein) against vault strings, and matches are masked automatically.
- Regex for plates, house numbers and phone numbers visible on signs.

W3 NANO PRE-SCREEN of the ORIGINAL photo (class S1, ONLY_ON_DEVICE)
- Prompt 1: a 768 px JPEG plus a JSON schema, returning {clues:[{type: enum[name_text, house_number, plate, street_sign, transit_sign, uniform_or_lanyard, crest_or_logo, mail_or_document, screen, window_view, reflection, landmark], text, region: enum(3x3 grid), severity: enum}]}.
- Prompt 2: vault LABELS (never coordinates) plus the OCR strings, asking which visible items correspond to vault entries; returns enum matches.
- Nano and Tesseract act as two independent readers; either one is enough to trigger a mask.
- Strict mode masks every flagged clue before the cloud sees anything.
- Without Nano: Tier-0 only, labelled "rules-only pre-screen".

W4 NANO REFEREE (class S0, ONLY_ON_DEVICE, text-only JSON)
- Input: the adversary's structured inferences (up to 12) plus vault labels. Output: {matches:[{claim_id, vault_id, strength: enum[exact, likely, possible, none], reason}]}. Example: "lanyard logo: City General Hospital" matches vault "work: City General".
- Distance is NOT an LLM job. Code computes haversine distance from each cloud hypothesis (lat, lng, radius) to each vault pin and assigns a band: <=250 m street, <=1 km neighbourhood, <=5 km district, same city, same country, none.
- Without Nano: a deterministic fuzzy and synonym matcher, labelled "rules-only referee".

W5 NANO FIX PLANNER AND EXPLAINER (S0, ONLY_ON_DEVICE, 256 output tokens or fewer)
- Chooses the smallest set of clue boxes whose removal breaks the matched inferences, orders them, and explains in plain language, e.g. "The lanyard and the stop code led to your workplace; the paving alone only reveals the country."
- Without Nano: mask every clue the adversary marked as removable.

W6 MASK AND EXPORT (code)
- Solid fills, never Gaussian blur, because blurred digits can be recovered. Boxes are padded 15%. Optional crop.
- EXIF-free re-encode, then download or share.

W7 EGRESS GATE (code). Every Firebase AI Logic call goes through one wrapper, which:
- (a) refuses S0 or S1 payloads on any mode that can reach the cloud;
- (b) re-checks the outgoing bitmap: 0 faces detected, 0 OCR matches against the vault, no EXIF;
- (c) scans the prompt text for vault strings;
- (d) writes a Cloud Ledger entry: bytes, payload class, model, inferenceSource, latency.
- Any failed check blocks the call with a toast naming the item: "Blocked: 'LUCAS' would have left this device."

5. ON-DEVICE JOBS: iOS (SwiftUI, FirebaseAILogic 12.13+ via SPM, Apple Foundation Models)
Apple FM on iOS has no image input and no on-device structured output, so Vision handles the pixels and the LLM works on text.
- I1 VAULT: CoreLocation "pin this place", plus names, plates and employer. Stored in Keychain with Data Protection 'complete'. Never synced.
- I2 TIER-0
  - Re-encode with CGImageDestination without metadata.
  - VNDetectFaceRectanglesRequest feeds the face masks.
  - VNRecognizeTextRequest produces word boxes for fuzzy vault matching.
  - VNClassifyImageRequest supplies scene labels.
- I3 FM PRE-SCREEN (S1)
  - Vision text plus scene labels plus vault labels go to an ON-DEVICE-ONLY session: the system model WITHOUT HybridModel, which throws instead of falling back. Verify on Day 1.
  - Output comes through a reportClue(...) tool call if on-device function calling passes the Day-1 spike. Otherwise use a strict one-item-per-line format, validated in code with one retry.
- I4 FM REFEREE AND FIX PLANNER (S0, on-device-only session)
  - Same contract as W4/W5, with every prompt budgeted under 4,096 tokens: up to 20 short vault labels, up to 12 claims, no coordinates. Distance bands are computed in code.
- I5 EXPLAINER (S2): HybridModel(primary: SystemLanguageModel.default, secondary: Gemini) answers "why does this clue reveal location?". The content is public, so real automatic cloud fallback is allowed and shown.
- I6 Core Image solid-fill masks, save to Photos, and the same Egress Gate and Ledger in Swift. The inference-source badge reads from the response (rawResponse.modelVersion per the docs; verify on Day 1).

6. CLOUD JOBS (ONLY_IN_CLOUD via Firebase AI Logic)
Settings: a Gemini vision model named in Remote Config (e.g. gemini-3.8-flash), temperature 0, on the paid no-training tier or the Vertex AI backend (whichever supports hybrid; check on Day 1).
- C1 ADVERSARY PASS A (grounded, streamed)
  - Input: ONLY the redacted, EXIF-free copy, with faces and vault matches already masked.
  - Prompt: a privacy audit commissioned by the photo's owner. Analyse the scene, never people; list every location-revealing clue; reason toward a location.
  - Google Search grounding is on, e.g. to confirm a logo or a transit-stop code. The investigator notes stream with the required Search Suggestions chip and source links.
- C2 ADVERSARY PASS B (structured, no grounding, because grounding plus a JSON schema in one call is flaky)
  - Input: the image plus pass A's notes.
  - Output: {hypotheses:[{label, lat, lng, radius_km, confidence: enum}] (at most 3), clues:[{id, type, box_2d [ymin,xmin,ymax,xmax] 0-1000, evidence, removable: bool}], inferences:[{id, kind: enum[workplace, school, home_area, routine, transit_line, venue, other], value}]}.
- C3 RE-ATTACK: C1 and C2 run again on the fixed image; the device compares the results.
- The cloud NEVER receives the vault, any pin, any name, unmasked faces, EXIF, the original photo, or the referee's verdict. It cannot learn whether it was right.
- Why the cloud: world-scale visual knowledge plus live Search. A ~3B on-device model cannot geolocate a street.

7. ROUTING POLICY (Remote Config key routing_policy; drawn live in the Router HUD)
| Class | What it covers | Web mode | iOS mode | Fallback |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S0 | Touches the vault (referee, fix plan, vault match) | ONLY_ON_DEVICE | On-device-only session | Deterministic code; NEVER cloud |
| S1 | Original, unredacted photo | ONLY_ON_DEVICE | On-device-only session | Tier-0; NEVER cloud |
| S2 | Redacted public pixels or public text after consent (clue explanations, optional second-opinion clue pass) | PREFER_ON_DEVICE | HybridModel | Real automatic cloud fallback, shown with an IN_CLOUD badge |
| S3 | Adversary | ONLY_IN_CLOUD | ONLY_IN_CLOUD | None |
| S4 | Synthetic sample gallery | PREFER_ON_DEVICE | PREFER_ON_DEVICE | Cloud, so judges without Nano see every AI step |
The Egress Gate enforces the class at runtime. The policy lives as data in Remote Config, not as scattered if-statements.

8. SIGNATURE DEMO MOMENT
- Split screen. Left: the photo and the verdict. Right: the Cloud Ledger, with counters "Faces sent: 0 · Vault items sent: 0".
- The red verdict appears: "Identified your WORKPLACE by name · Home: within 1 km · Child's name: caught and masked on this device". The device referee computes it while the Ledger still reads 0.
- A deliberate leak attempt (un-mask the name tag, re-send) is BLOCKED by the Egress Gate.
- One tap on Fix (on-device), then re-attack: "Country only, low confidence", and the verdict turns green: "Risk reduced".
- Closing line: "The stalker never learns it was right."

9. FEATURES
MVP (all done by Nov 28):
- Web PWA:
  - capability panel;
  - vault;
  - import by file, drag or paste (no URL input);
  - Tier-0 guard and Nano pre-screen;
  - a consent sheet showing the exact redacted image that will leave;
  - adversary C1/C2 with streaming notes and grounding chips;
  - referee with distance bands;
  - verdict card with red, amber and green lines, showing bands, never metres;
  - fix planner, masking and re-attack;
  - Cloud Ledger, Egress Gate and a "What the cloud saw" toggle;
  - Router HUD showing inferenceSource and latency for every call;
  - download of the cleaned photo, and a share card with no location;
  - Judge Mode;
  - offline mode: the PWA is cached, the vault, pre-screen and fix work with Wi-Fi off, and the cloud check waits in a queue until online.
- iOS: vault, PHPicker import, Vision Tier-0, FM pre-screen/referee/fix plan (on-device-only), HybridModel explainer, cloud adversary, masking, Ledger, and the same Remote Config policy.
- Benchmark: 25 photos (see section 14).
STRETCH (only if Day 9 is green, in this order):
1. Chrome extension "check before you post", a thin catcher for ONE site with a standard file input. A capture-phase change listener hands the file to the hosted PWA via externally_connectable messaging, and the cleaned file is swapped back with DataTransfer. No Firebase inside the extension, so no App Check problem.
2. iOS Share Extension: writes to an App Group and the main app does the analysis.
3. Any-language explanations: the cloud translates explanation TEMPLATES containing placeholders ({{WORKPLACE}}, {{HOME}}), and the device fills them in.
4. Batch "check my last 20 posts".
CUT: Android, URL or scraping input, map pins of the adversary's guess, children's faces sent to the cloud, and any "safe" claims.

10. PLATFORMS
- WEB (primary; the surface judges try; Best Web/Chrome): Vite + React + TypeScript PWA on Firebase Hosting, Firebase JS SDK firebase/ai hybrid, self-hosted MediaPipe tasks-vision and Tesseract.js.
- iOS (the on-device showcase; Best iOS; multi-platform consideration for the Grand Prize): SwiftUI, FirebaseAILogic, Vision, Core Image, CoreLocation. FM runs in the Simulator on this M1. The Simulator has no camera, so photos come in through Photos import.
- ANDROID: not built. One roadmap line notes that the same Firebase project could serve a cloud-path client.

11. FIREBASE PRODUCTS
- AI LOGIC hybrid inference:
  - the per-class modes above;
  - inferenceSource drives the badges;
  - cloud Gemini with image input and Google Search grounding;
  - AI Logic per-user rate limits.
- APP CHECK, enforced:
  - reCAPTCHA Enterprise on the hosted web app;
  - App Attest on iOS devices, and the debug provider in the Simulator;
  - it also throttles abuse of the adversary.
- ANONYMOUS AUTH: per-user quotas without collecting any identity.
- REMOTE CONFIG, cached for offline use:
  - routing_policy;
  - prompt versions (adversary A and B, referee, fix planner);
  - model names and temperature;
  - distance-band thresholds and the clue-type enum;
  - daily cap on adversary runs and feature flags (grounding, extension);
  - a global cloud kill switch.
- FIRESTORE:
  - (a) "Leak Atlas": opt-in, anonymous counters by clue TYPE plus whether the fix moved the distance band. No images, coordinates, vault data or per-photo documents. Increments are validated by security rules. Shown as "Most common giveaways this week". These counters go to Firestore, never to Gemini.
  - (b) Judge Mode sample metadata, plus cached pass-B (ungrounded) outputs for the synthetic samples only. Grounded output is never cached across users.
- HOSTING: the PWA and the sample assets.
- NOTE: AI Monitoring cannot see on-device calls, so the Ledger keeps its own local counters.

12. SAFETY AND LIMITS
- CHILDREN: faces are always masked before any cloud call, and the demo photos contain no people.
- REFUSALS: privacy-auditor framing, scene only. If Gemini declines, show "Adversary declined; on-device findings only" and keep the local result. Never retry with jailbreak phrasing.
- DUAL USE
  - Only files from the user's own device; no URL input.
  - The UI shows distance bands to YOUR pins and clue boxes only, never a map pin or address for the guess.
  - App Check, AI Logic per-user limits, and a Remote Config cap plus kill switch.
  - The README says honestly that the raw JSON is visible in DevTools and that the added harm over the public Gemini app is close to zero.
- CLAIMS: say "risk reduced", never "safe"; use bands, never metre-level precision; always show confidence.
- DATA
  - No-training tier.
  - Consent for every photo, with the exact outgoing image shown.
  - A Ledger receipt for every session.
  - A "burn vault" button.
  - Solid-fill masks; the output is re-OCR'd and must contain no vault text.
- GROUNDING TERMS: render Search Suggestions and sources with the grounded notes; never cache grounded output across users.
- TOKEN LIMITS
  - iOS prompts stay under 4,096 tokens and Nano prompts under 9,216.
  - Outputs are short.
  - The iOS app works in the foreground only.
- LANGUAGES
  - Vision OCR and Gemini are multilingual.
  - Nano accepts en/es/ja (plus de/fr where available), so on-device prompts are English templates wrapped around the extracted strings.
  - Apple FM covers more languages.
- FILMING: never the builder's real home or a real primary school. Use a fictional name tag, a prop lanyard with a logo, and a "home" pin on a public building near the shoot.

13. GRACEFUL DEGRADATION (judges without on-device AI)
- A first-run capability panel calls availability() and shows what runs where on THIS browser.
- With no Nano (Safari, Firefox, mobile, low-RAM laptops, or the model still downloading), the app runs the Tier-0 guard, the cloud adversary and the deterministic referee.
  - The full red-to-green loop still works.
  - The privacy guarantee does not change: the original photo never leaves the device.
  - Badges read "rules-only" instead of "Gemini Nano".
- JUDGE MODE: one click loads 3 synthetic scenes and a fake vault, routed as S4. Every AI step runs, lands IN_CLOUD with honest badges, and goes from red to green in about 60 s.
- TRY YOUR OWN: drop in your last Instagram post with an empty vault and you still get the clue map and the adversary's region.
- iOS: video plus build instructions. A TestFlight public link only if a paid developer account exists and review is started by Nov 26.

14. MEASURED, NOT CLAIMED (benchmark in the repo)
- Photo set: 25 builder-owned, people-free photos with known true locations.
- Measure:
  - the share of photos placed within 1 km and within 5 km, before and after the fix;
  - the refusal rate;
  - pre-screen recall for Nano vs Tier-0 vs cloud, on hand-labelled clues;
  - p50 and p95 latency for each tier;
  - on-device vs cloud call counts per session.
- Publish whatever the numbers turn out to be.

15. BUILD PLAN (deadline Dec 1 00:00 GMT+2)
D1 (Nov 19-20): go/no-go spikes.
- (a) Adversary on 10 of the builder's own photos through AI Logic (image plus grounding, then the schema pass). PASS if there are at most 2 refusals and at least 4 photos land within 5 km.
- (b) Nano with image input and a JSON schema through the Firebase hybrid SDK in Chrome 157 on this 8 GB M1 (check chrome://on-device-internals).
- (c) iOS 27 Simulator: on-device-only session, HybridModel, and a tool call.
- If (a) fails, switch to Blindfill on D2; the router, Egress Gate and Ledger code carry over.
- If (b) fails, iOS carries the on-device story and the web shows Tier-0 plus cloud honestly.
D2-D5 (Nov 21-24): web core loop.
D6 (Nov 25): App Check, Auth, Remote Config, Firestore, Judge Mode, Hosting.
D7-D9 (Nov 26-28): iOS app, plus the benchmark run.
D10 (Nov 29): polish, README, stretch features only if green. Record each beat separately and never run Simulator FM and Chrome Nano together on 8 GB.
D11 (Nov 30): edit the video, write the Devpost text, submit.

synthesis.why_beats_baseline:
WHY THE EARLIER PLAN LEANED ON HEALTH
- The scoring rewarded the two textbook reasons for running AI on-device: data that can't legally leave the device, and connectivity you can't rely on. Clinical notes in low-connectivity clinics are the most literal example of both.
- That same logic is why the plan failed review:
  - It is the most obvious privacy story, so it is crowded (ambient scribes, the Penda/OpenAI AI Consult study, Presidio-style redactors).
  - It is tied to one region.
  - Its on-device path doesn't run on the hardware its users own: low-resource clinics rarely have Nano-capable Chrome or Apple Intelligence devices.
  - PREFER_ON_DEVICE quietly sent raw patient data to the cloud whenever no local model existed.
- The red team's verdict on the baseline was "kill".

SCORING METHOD
- Start with the mean of the 4 official criteria.
- Add 0.15 per point for demo wow, global reach and judge tryability above 7 (subtract the same per point below 7).
- Add 0.1 per point for hybrid honesty above 6 (subtract below 6).
- Subtract 0.1 per point for crowdedness above 5 and feasibility risk above 6 (add the same per point below).
- Red-team verdict: viable 0, risky -0.2, kill -0.6.
- Specific fatal flaws carry their own penalty, e.g. Blindfill's collision with Google's own autofill, or Utter's prior winner in Google's Chrome Built-in AI Challenge.
- Result: Strangers' Eyes 8.18 vs Muganga 5.00.

HOW STRANGERS' EYES COMPARES WITH THE BASELINE
| | Strangers' Eyes | Muganga |
|---|---|---|
| Judge average | 7.9 | 6.5 |
| Global reach | 9 | 5 |
| Demo wow | 8 | 6 |
| Crowdedness | 4 | 6 |
| Red-team verdict | viable | kill |

WHY IT WINS
1. It is global by construction. Everyone posts photos, and the threat (pixel-level geolocation) and the fix are identical in every country. It is not a health product.
2. The hybrid split comes from the problem itself. The cloud has world-scale visual knowledge and Search, which a 3B model cannot match. The device holds secrets the cloud must never see. The cloud attacker never learns whether it was right. That is the non-obvious use of Firebase AI Logic that Quality of Idea rewards, not "on-device if available, else cloud".
3. Judges can actually try it. Without Nano, the Tier-0 guard, the cloud adversary and the deterministic referee still run the full red-to-green loop, and the guarantee that the original photo never leaves still holds. The baseline's privacy path simply disappears on judges' machines.
4. It uses all of the SDK honestly:
   - ONLY_ON_DEVICE for the vault and the raw photo, failing closed to deterministic code;
   - PREFER_ON_DEVICE with real automatic fallback for public content;
   - ONLY_IN_CLOUD with image input and Search grounding for the attacker;
   - inferenceSource shown on every call;
   - on iOS, HybridModel for public tasks and an on-device-only session for sensitive ones.
5. The demo is visceral and easy to understand in 10 seconds: an AI "stalker" finds you, the gate blocks a leak, one tap fixes it, and a re-attack confirms. Compare a 3-minute video of SOAP notes.
6. It fits the hardware. The core loop is a web PWA plus an iOS app whose on-device path runs in the Simulator on this M1. No Android phone is needed, and no clinical validation is required.
synthesis.key_risks_and_mitigations:
1. GEMINI REFUSES OR HEDGES on the geolocation prompt.
- Frame the prompt as a privacy audit commissioned by the photo's owner, about the scene only. Faces are masked before the call.
- Go/no-go on Day 1 using 10 of the builder's own people-free photos: pass with at most 2 refusals and at least 4 placed within 5 km.
- In the app, a refusal shows "on-device findings only" and is never retried with jailbreak phrasing.
- If the Day-1 check fails, switch to Blindfill on Day 2, reusing the router, Egress Gate and Ledger.

2. GEOLOCATION QUALITY IS UNEVEN AND NON-DETERMINISTIC. It is weaker outside well-photographed cities, and a re-attack can still guess the location from architecture.
- Temperature 0 and a pinned model through Remote Config.
- Show distance bands and confidence, never metres.
- Say "risk reduced", never "safe". Offer cropping when masking isn't enough.
- Publish honest benchmark numbers.
- Pre-test the exact demo photos 10 or more times.

3. THE PRIVACY STORY CONTRADICTS ITSELF if the cloud sees the photo.
- The cloud only ever gets a copy with faces masked, vault matches masked and EXIF stripped.
- Strict mode masks every clue flagged on-device.
- The consent sheet shows the exact outgoing image, and the Egress Gate re-checks it.
- Use a no-training paid tier or the Vertex backend.
- The claim: "the cloud sees the redacted photo you were about to publish, and 0 bytes from your vault."

4. THE HYBRID LOOKS THIN (it could look like string matching plus a distance calculation).
- Give Nano and FM real semantic work: reading leaks from the raw image, matching inferences to the vault ("lanyard logo" to "work: City General"), and the minimal fix plan with an explanation.
- Say openly that the distance math is deterministic on purpose.
- Use S2 PREFER_ON_DEVICE so the SDK's automatic fallback is visible.
- Show inferenceSource on every call.

5. CHROME NANO ON THE 8 GB M1 IS UNVERIFIED (Chrome asks for 16 GB of RAM or more than 4 GB of VRAM).
- The v3Nano weights are reportedly already downloaded on this Mac; confirm on Day 1.
- If Nano won't run, iOS FM carries the on-device footage, and the web build shows Tier-0 plus the cloud honestly.
- Never run the Simulator's FM and Chrome Nano at the same time; record each video beat separately.

6. THE EXPERIMENTAL iOS SDK (on-device-only session, on-device function calling, reading the inference source) is unverified.
- Spike all three on Day 1.
- If function calling fails, use a strict line format parsed and validated in code, with one retry.
- Any direct use of native FoundationModels is disclosed and limited to a fallback.

7. DUAL USE (someone saves a stranger's photo and runs it).
- Local files only, no URLs.
- The UI shows only bands relative to YOUR pins and clue boxes, never a map pin or address for the guess.
- App Check, AI Logic per-user limits, a Remote Config daily cap and a kill switch.
- The README states plainly that the raw JSON is visible in DevTools and that the added harm over the public Gemini app is close to zero.

8. PRIOR ART: arXiv 2503.20226 and Geo-Safe-Filter already do warn, blur, re-check.
- Cite both.
- Lead with what is new: the vault acts as private ground truth, the referee never tells the attacker, the egress gate is enforced, and routing is by sensitivity class.
- The headline line is "the stalker never learns it was right."

9. SCOPE FOR ONE AGENT IN 11 DAYS.
- Order: web loop, then Firebase hardening, then iOS, then benchmark, then stretch.
- The Chrome extension and the iOS Share Extension are stretch goals only.
- Android is cut.

10. GROUNDING ISSUES: the Search-grounding terms, and a single call that combines grounding with a JSON schema is flaky.
- Use two passes: grounded notes that render Search Suggestions and sources, then an ungrounded structured pass.
- Never cache grounded output across users.

11. THE DEMO COULD DOX THE BUILDER, or create bad optics around children.
- Never film the builder's real home or a real primary school.
- Use a fictional "LUCAS" tag, a prop lanyard with a logo, and a public building as the "home" pin.
- No people in any photo.

12. JUDGES CAN'T INSTALL THE iOS APP.
- iOS is judged mainly from the video.
- Start TestFlight review by Nov 26 only if a paid developer account exists.
- The web Judge Mode carries hands-on testing.
synthesis.storyboard:
RULES FOR THE WHOLE VIDEO
- A Router HUD in the bottom-left logs every call, e.g. "pre-screen > ON-DEVICE (Gemini Nano) 2.1 s", "adversary > IN_CLOUD (Gemini + Search) 6 s", "referee > ON-DEVICE 1.3 s".
- The Cloud Ledger sits on the right with the counters "Faces sent: 0 · Vault items sent: 0".
- All photos are people-free and shot in the builder's own city. The "home" pin is a public building near the shoot. Props: a fictional "LUCAS" name tag and a lanyard with a logo but no text.
- Wi-Fi is toggled visibly in the macOS menu bar, because the Simulator has no airplane mode.
- Record each beat separately, using real measured numbers only.

BEAT 1 (0:00-0:18) HOOK
- Full-screen doorstep photo: a backpack with a name tag, a lanyard on a hook, a street sign and a bus stop behind.
- Caption: "This photo has no GPS data."
- Investigator notes stream in, sped up: "Bus stop code... street sign... lanyard logo..."
- The verdict bar turns red: "Home: within 1 km."
- VO: "Deleting location data doesn't protect you anymore. AI reads the street."
- Title card: STRANGERS' EYES, "See your photo the way a stalker's AI would, before you post it."

BEAT 2 (0:18-0:35) THE VAULT, iOS Simulator in an iPhone frame
- "Pin this place" for Home, then Work (City General), then the child's name "Lucas".
- Lock badge: "Stays on this device. Never geocoded. Never uploaded."
- The Ledger shows 0 requests.
- One caption line: parents, sellers, creators, survivors, in any country.

BEAT 3 (0:35-0:58) OFFLINE PRE-SCREEN, Chrome PWA with Wi-Fi visibly OFF
- Drop in the photo. An ON-DEVICE (Gemini Nano) badge appears, plus a Tier-0 chip.
- Flag: "LUCAS on backpack matches your child's name." The tag and the house number get solid masks.
- The lanyard logo is flagged amber: "possible identifier".
- Chip: "Deeper check queued until you're online."

BEAT 4 (0:58-1:40) RED TEAM, the centrepiece
- Wi-Fi back on. The consent sheet shows the exact masked image: "This, and only this, will be sent."
- The IN_CLOUD badge lights. Notes stream with Search source chips, and evidence boxes land on the stop code, the street sign and the lanyard logo.
- "Referee comparing guesses with your vault... on this device" (ON-DEVICE badge).
- The verdict turns red:
  - "Identified your WORKPLACE by name"
  - "Home: within 1 km"
  - "Child's name: caught and masked before upload"
- 4-second split graphic: the cloud sees masked pixels, the device holds the truth. "The cloud never learns it was right."
- The Ledger still reads 0 / 0.

BEAT 5 (1:40-1:55) THE GATE
- The user un-ticks the name-tag mask and taps re-check.
- A red toast: "Blocked: 'LUCAS' would have left this device."
- The "What the cloud saw" toggle shows only the masked copy.

BEAT 6 (1:55-2:20) FIX AND RE-ATTACK
- Tap Fix. The on-device plan reads: "Mask the lanyard and the stop code; the paving alone only reveals the country."
- Solid fills animate in. The re-attack runs IN_CLOUD and returns "Country-level, low confidence".
- The verdict turns green: "Risk reduced" (never "safe").
- Receipt: "Cloud received 2 redacted images · 0 faces · 0 vault items · 9 on-device calls."
- The share card appears, with no location.

BEAT 7 (2:20-2:42) PROOF AND PLATFORMS
- Benchmark card with the real numbers: "25 photos: located within 1 km before fix X/25, after fix Y/25; refusals Z."
- iOS cameo: the same verdict with an Apple Foundation Models badge, and Vision drawing the masks.
- Routing table overlay:
  - vault and original photo: ONLY_ON_DEVICE
  - public explanations: PREFER_ON_DEVICE, falling back to the cloud
  - attacker: ONLY_IN_CLOUD

BEAT 8 (2:42-3:00) CLOSE
- Firebase stack strip: AI Logic hybrid, App Check, Remote Config, Anonymous Auth, Firestore, Hosting.
- "Try it in any browser, no on-device AI needed: sample gallery, 60 seconds."
- VO: "Stalkers already have this AI. Now you do too, and it never learns where you live."
- URL and repo link.
synthesis.runner_up: Blindfill: the cloud reads the form, only your device reads you
synthesis.runner_up_summary:
Composite score 7.98. This is a close second and the Day-2 fallback if the Strangers' Eyes adversary fails its Day-1 go/no-go.

WHAT IT IS
- Understanding a form is public knowledge; the answers are private.
- The cloud (Gemini with PDF input, long context and Search grounding) reads only BLANK official forms and their guidance notes. It turns them into "form cards" stored in a shared Firestore library (written by a Cloud Function, with sources), so the next person anywhere filling the same form makes zero LLM calls.
- The device does the private half:
  - builds a vault from passport and ID photos, using Nano image-to-JSON plus a deterministic ICAO MRZ checksum as a second reader;
  - lets the user answer in their own language and fills fields in the form's format;
  - runs cross-document consistency checks (e.g. the passport expires too soon after return);
  - shows a Cloud Ledger proving 0 personal fields were sent.
- Audience: about 304M migrants, students and visa applicants worldwide.

WHY IT LOST
- Higher raw judge average (8.1), but crowdedness 6 and feasibility risk 7: three surfaces, pdf-lib, the card pipeline, and XFA and portal forms shrinking the usable target set.
- Many existing Nano form fillers.
- It collides head-on with Google's own Chrome enhanced autofill and "Find and fill with Gemini" (US, Oct 28 2026), in front of Google judges.
- Its private vault runs ONLY_ON_DEVICE, so most judges would only see a cloud demo persona.
- Much of the on-device work (MRZ, formatting) is deterministic, which makes the AI look decorative.

IF SWITCHING TO IT
- Keep the web PWA and iOS; drop the MV3 extension.
- Choose verified AcroForm forms that are genuinely global (e.g. IRS W-8BEN plus one Schengen consulate PDF).
- Make the sensitivity router the hero: public questions use PREFER_ON_DEVICE, private ones ONLY_ON_DEVICE.
- Position it as complementary to Chrome autofill: "Autofill knows your passport number; it doesn't know what Geburtsname means or which section applies to you."
- The Egress Gate, Ledger and Remote Config routing code built for Strangers' Eyes carries over unchanged.
